abstract: We prove that the fundamental group of every smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety that is special in the sense of Campana is virtually nilpotent of class at most two. This establishes the two-step nilpotency conjecture of Cao--Deng--Hacon--P\u{a}un, a quasi-projective analogue of Campana's almost abelian conjecture for special compact K\"ahler manifolds. Examples of Cadorel--Deng--Yamanoi show that the step bound is sharp. On a suitable finite etale cover, we construct a canonical second Albanese map to a torus torsor over an abelian variety. The proof reduces to showing that the kernel of the induced map on fundamental groups is finite. Using good minimal models and meridian groups of projective pairs, we show that an infinite kernel would yield a saturated rank-one subsheaf of logarithmic differentials whose Iitaka dimension contradicts specialness.
hook: Fundamental groups of special quasi-projective varieties are virtually nilpotent of class at most two.
summary: The paper proves a conjecture of Cao, Deng, Hacon and Paun: the fundamental group of a special quasi-projective complex variety, in Campana's sense, has a nilpotent subgroup of finite index and class at most two. Known examples show two cannot be lowered. The proof builds a second Albanese map and shows its kernel on fundamental groups is finite, using minimal models. It is a highly specialized result that applies only to special varieties.
title: Virtual Two-Step Nilpotency of the Fundamental Groups of Special Quasi-Projective Varieties
